Spark's full account of an error

spark_error_details.Rd

A zuspark_sql_error carries Spark's error class, SQLSTATE, message parameters and the exception's class hierarchy. spark_error_details() asks the server for the rest, through FetchErrorDetails: every exception in the cause chain, with its stack trace and the places in the query it points at. The server keeps these only for a while, and only when spark.sql.connect.enrichError.enabled is on (the default).

Usage

spark_error_details(err, con = err$con)

Arguments

err

A zuspark_sql_error, as caught with tryCatch().

con

The connection to ask; by default the one the error came from.

Value

A list with one element per exception, the root first. Each is a list of type (the class hierarchy), message, error_class, sql_state, message_parameters, cause (the index of its cause in the list, or NA), stack (a data frame of class, method, file and line) and contexts (a data frame of the query fragments).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # nzchar(Sys.getenv("SPARK_REMOTE"))
con <- spark_connect()
err <- tryCatch(spark_sql(con, "SELECT * FROM no_such_table"), error = identity)
err$error_class
details <- spark_error_details(err)
details[[1]]$message
spark_disconnect(con)
}
